questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was established under the RBI Act in the year:
questions.explanation: The RBI was constituted on 1 April 1935 under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934. 1926 was the year the Hilton-Young Commission recommended its creation, not the establishment. 1947 is India's Independence year. 1949 is when the RBI was nationalized, not when it was originally established.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Indian economy:

(i) India is classified as a mixed economy with both public and private sectors.
(ii) The five-year plans in India followed the Soviet model.
(iii) The Planning Commission was replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015.
(iv) India's fiscal year runs from January 1 to December 31.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i), (ii), (iii) are correct. India runs a mixed economy, its five-year plans drew from Soviet-style planning, and NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission on 1 January 2015. (iv) is INCORRECT — India's fiscal year runs from 1 April to 31 March, not the calendar year. Any option including (iv) is therefore wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: GDP stands for:
questions.explanation: GDP = Gross Domestic Product — the total monetary value of goods and services produced within a country's borders in a given period. 'Gross Development Programme' is invented. 'General Domestic Policy' is not a standard acronym. 'Government Development Plan' has no such abbreviation.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Reserve Bank of India uses the repo rate as a key tool of monetary policy.
Reason (R): By raising the repo rate, RBI makes borrowing more expensive for commercial banks, which tends to cool demand and inflation.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — the repo rate is the RBI's headline monetary-policy instrument. (R) is correct — a repo hike raises banks' borrowing costs, transmitting to loan rates and dampening demand and inflation. (R) explains (A) directly. Option 2 wrongly denies the explanatory link. Options 3 and 4 wrongly deny (A) or (R).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Green Revolution' in India, associated with the widespread adoption of high-yielding varieties of seeds, is chiefly linked with:
questions.explanation: M. S. Swaminathan is called the 'Father of the Green Revolution in India' — he led the introduction of high-yielding wheat and rice varieties from the 1960s. Verghese Kurien led the WHITE Revolution (Operation Flood / dairy). Amartya Sen is a Nobel-laureate economist known for welfare economics, not agriculture. Manmohan Singh led the 1991 LPG reforms, unrelated to agricultural revolution.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following economic terms with their definitions:

Column I:
(a) Inflation
(b) Deflation
(c) Stagflation
(d) Recession

Column II:
(i) A general fall in the price level over time
(ii) A general rise in the price level over time
(iii) A combination of high inflation and slow economic growth
(iv) A significant decline in economic activity lasting more than a few months

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Inflation = rising prices → (a)-(ii). Deflation = falling prices → (b)-(i). Stagflation = high inflation + slow growth (a 1970s puzzle) → (c)-(iii). Recession = declining activity → (d)-(iv). The distractor (a)-(i) swaps inflation with deflation. (c)-(iv) swaps stagflation with recession. (a)-(iii) misclassifies inflation as stagflation.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Fiscal Deficit' of a country is best defined as:
options: The amount of foreign debt owed by the government
The difference between exports and imports
The amount of currency in circulation
The gap between government revenue and expenditure
questions.correctAnswer: The gap between government revenue and expenditure
questions.explanation: Fiscal deficit = total expenditure − total revenue (excluding borrowings), representing the government's borrowing requirement. Foreign debt is a separate concept (external debt). Difference between exports and imports is the trade balance / trade deficit — not the fiscal deficit. Currency in circulation is a monetary aggregate, not a fiscal concept.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) in India?

(i) SAIL (Steel Authority of India Limited)
(ii) ONGC (Oil and Natural Gas Corporation)
(iii) BHEL (Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited)
(iv) Reliance Industries

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: SAIL, ONGC and BHEL are all central PSUs owned significantly by the Government of India. Reliance Industries is a PRIVATE-sector company controlled by the Ambani family — not a PSU. Any option including (iv) is therefore wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The main objective of the Goods and Services Tax (GST), implemented in India from July 2017, was to:
options: Replace multiple indirect taxes with a unified national tax
Impose direct income tax on all citizens
questions.correctAnswer: Replace multiple indirect taxes with a unified national tax
questions.explanation: GST subsumed multiple central and state indirect taxes (excise, service tax, VAT, entry tax, etc.) into a single unified indirect tax on goods and services. Increasing corporate profits is not the stated objective. GST is an INDIRECT tax, not a direct income tax. Farmer subsidies are provided through separate schemes like MSP and PM-KISAN, not GST.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Nabard (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) was established in the year:
questions.explanation: NABARD was established on 12 July 1982 under the NABARD Act, 1981, as the apex development bank for agriculture and rural credit. 1969 was the year of bank nationalization (14 banks). 1980 was the second round of bank nationalization (6 more banks). 1991 was the year of economic liberalization (LPG reforms).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The __________ is the highest measure of a country's economic size, including all goods and services produced within its borders in a year.
questions.explanation: GDP (Gross Domestic Product) measures the total output of a country. Per Capita Income is GDP per person, a derived measure. Fiscal Deficit is a government-budget concept, not a measure of economic size. Wholesale Price Index measures price inflation, not output.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Repo Rate' in Indian monetary policy is the rate at which:
options: Commercial banks lend money to individuals
Commercial banks borrow money from the RBI against government securities
The government pays interest on public debt
The RBI lends money to state governments
questions.correctAnswer: Commercial banks borrow money from the RBI against government securities
questions.explanation: Repo rate is the rate at which the RBI provides short-term liquidity to commercial banks against collateral (usually government securities). Retail lending rates to individuals are set by banks themselves, based on repo but not identical. Interest on public debt refers to bond yields, unrelated. RBI does not lend directly to state governments at the repo rate.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Indian budget:

(i) The Union Budget is presented in Parliament by the Finance Minister every year.
(ii) The Railway Budget was merged with the Union Budget in 2017.
(iii) The Union Budget contains estimates of revenue and expenditure for the ENTIRE year immediately following.
(iv) The Budget is presented on 15 August every year.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i), (ii), (iii) are all correct — the Finance Minister presents the Union Budget, the Railway Budget was merged in 2017, and the budget covers the coming fiscal year. (iv) is INCORRECT — the Union Budget is presented on 1 February (since 2017); previously it was on the last working day of February. 15 August is Independence Day, unrelated. Any option including (iv) is therefore wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'PMJDY' (Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana), launched in 2014, aims to:
options: Provide free housing to all citizens
Achieve universal financial inclusion through zero-balance bank accounts
Guarantee 100 days of employment to rural households
questions.correctAnswer: Achieve universal financial inclusion through zero-balance bank accounts
questions.explanation: PMJDY is India's flagship financial-inclusion scheme, providing zero-balance bank accounts, RuPay debit cards, insurance and overdraft facilities to hitherto unbanked households. Free housing is the aim of PMAY (Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana). 100 days of guaranteed employment is MGNREGA. Reducing corruption is not the primary aim of PMJDY (though DBT built on it helps).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India adopted a policy of Liberalization, Privatization and Globalization (LPG) in 1991.
Reason (R): The 1991 balance of payments crisis forced India to seek IMF assistance and undertake major economic reforms.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — LPG reforms were launched under P.V. Narasimha Rao's government with Manmohan Singh as FM in 1991. (R) is correct — the 1991 BoP crisis (foreign reserves depleted to a few weeks' imports) forced India to approach the IMF for assistance and undertake structural reforms. (R) directly explains (A) — LPG reforms were the answer to the crisis (R describes). Option 2 wrongly denies the explanatory link. Options 3 and 4 wrongly deny (A) or (R).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'CRR' (Cash Reserve Ratio) is the percentage of:
options: Foreign exchange reserves held by the RBI
GDP that is spent on defence
Total taxes collected by the central government
A bank's net demand and time liabilities that must be maintained as cash with the RBI
questions.correctAnswer: A bank's net demand and time liabilities that must be maintained as cash with the RBI
questions.explanation: CRR = percentage of a bank's NDTL kept as cash reserves with the RBI. Forex reserves of the RBI are a separate metric. GDP defence share is measured in the Union Budget, not called CRR. Central tax collection is a fiscal metric, unrelated to CRR.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Indian rupee was decimalized (with 100 paise = 1 rupee) in the year:
questions.explanation: The Indian rupee was decimalized on 1 April 1957 — before that, 1 rupee = 16 annas = 64 paise. 1947 is Independence, unrelated to currency decimalization. 1969 is bank nationalization. 1991 is LPG reforms.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are Direct Taxes in India?

(i) Income Tax
(ii) Corporate Tax
(iii) Goods and Services Tax (GST)
(iv) Customs Duty

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Direct taxes are levied directly on individuals/corporations — Income Tax (on individuals) and Corporate Tax (on companies) are the main direct taxes. GST is an INDIRECT tax on goods and services. Customs Duty is an INDIRECT tax on imports/exports. So only (i) and (ii) qualify as direct taxes. Any option including (iii) or (iv) is therefore wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The MSP (Minimum Support Price) system in India is used to:
options: Cap the retail price of essential commodities
Ensure a guaranteed price to farmers for specified agricultural crops
Set the minimum wage for industrial workers
Determine the exchange rate of the Indian rupee
questions.correctAnswer: Ensure a guaranteed price to farmers for specified agricultural crops
questions.explanation: MSP guarantees a minimum price to farmers for notified crops (like paddy, wheat, pulses) if market prices fall below the announced level, procured through agencies like FCI. Retail price caps for essentials use the Essential Commodities Act, not MSP. Minimum wage is set by Ministry of Labour under wage laws. Exchange rates are managed by the RBI's forex operations.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'HDI' (Human Development Index) is published annually by:
questions.explanation: The Human Development Report (containing HDI) is published by the UNDP (United Nations Development Programme). The World Bank publishes GDP data, Doing Business rankings and Poverty statistics — not HDI. IMF publishes economic forecasts and country reports. WTO deals with international trade, not human development.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the 'Priority Sector Lending' norms of the RBI:

(i) Priority Sector includes agriculture, MSME, education, housing and export credit.
(ii) Scheduled commercial banks are required to lend a specified percentage of their credit to priority sectors.
(iii) Priority Sector norms do not apply to foreign banks operating in India.
(iv) Priority Sector Lending Certificates (PSLCs) allow banks to trade the priority sector obligation.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i), (ii) and (iv) are all correct as per RBI's Priority Sector Lending framework. (iii) is INCORRECT — Priority Sector Lending targets apply to Foreign Banks operating in India as well (with certain relaxations for banks with fewer branches). Any option including (iii) is therefore wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Blue Revolution' in India refers to increased production in:
questions.explanation: Blue Revolution = fisheries and aquaculture production growth (associated with Dr. Arun Krishnan and the Fish Farmers' Development Agencies). Wheat/rice growth is the Green Revolution. Milk is the White Revolution (Operation Flood, Verghese Kurien). Cotton has been called the 'Silver Fibre Revolution' in specific contexts.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following economic institutions with their headquarters:

Column I:
(a) RBI (Reserve Bank of India)
(b) SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India)
(c) SBI (State Bank of India)
(d) NITI Aayog

Column II:
(i) Mumbai
(ii) Mumbai
(iii) Mumbai
(iv) New Delhi

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: RBI, SEBI and SBI are all headquartered in Mumbai (a)-(i), (b)-(ii), (c)-(iii). NITI Aayog is headquartered in New Delhi (Sansad Marg) → (d)-(iv). The distractor (a)-(iv) puts RBI in Delhi. (a)-(ii) confuses the sequence but is still Mumbai-based; the answer is uniquely correct because each label i, ii, iii, iv corresponds to a specific slot in the correct mapping. Given all three Mumbai items map to (i), (ii), (iii) in order and NITI Aayog to (iv) Delhi, the first option is uniquely correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'National Income' of a country is the sum of:
options: GDP + Net factor income from abroad
questions.correctAnswer: GDP + Net factor income from abroad
questions.explanation: Broadly, GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad, and National Income (NNI at factor cost) is derived from GNP by subtracting depreciation and adjusting for taxes/subsidies. The closest option is GDP + Net factor income from abroad = GNP, which is the base for National Income. GDP − Depreciation gives NDP (Net Domestic Product), a different concept. GDP − Taxes is not a standard measure. GDP × Population is not a standard formula (Per Capita GDP is GDP / population).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The GST Council is a constitutional body established under Article 279A of the Constitution.
Reason (R): The 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016, inserted Article 279A to create the GST Council.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — the GST Council is constitutionally created under Article 279A. (R) is correct — the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016, inserted Article 279A and other GST-enabling provisions. (R) directly explains (A). Option 2 wrongly denies the explanatory link. Options 3 and 4 wrongly deny (A) or (R).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Twelfth Five Year Plan' of India (2012-2017) was the __________ five year plan.
questions.explanation: The Twelfth Five Year Plan (2012-2017) was the 12th in the series. It was also the LAST five-year plan (the practice of formal five-year plans was discontinued when the Planning Commission was replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015 — although the plan already in progress ran its full term to 2017). The 'Twelfth' answer is more directly descriptive; 'Last' is technically also true but doesn't answer the numerical designation.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Statutory Liquidity Ratio' (SLR) refers to:
options: The rate at which the RBI lends to commercial banks
The maximum interest rate on savings accounts
The percentage of a bank's shares held by the government
The minimum percentage of deposits a bank must maintain in liquid form (like cash, gold, or approved government securities)
questions.correctAnswer: The minimum percentage of deposits a bank must maintain in liquid form (like cash, gold, or approved government securities)
questions.explanation: SLR is the minimum percentage of Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL) that banks must maintain in liquid assets like cash, gold or approved government securities BEFORE providing credit. The rate at which RBI lends to banks is the Repo Rate. Interest rates on savings accounts are deregulated (banks set their own). Government shareholding % is unrelated to SLR.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: India's 'Look East Policy', later evolved into the 'Act East Policy', focuses on strengthening ties with:
questions.explanation: The Look East / Act East policy targets deeper economic and strategic engagement with Southeast Asia and East Asia (ASEAN countries, Japan, South Korea). EU relations are governed by separate strategic partnerships. Africa policy is guided by India-Africa Forum Summits. Gulf policy centers on 'Link West Policy' or bilateral MoUs, not Look East.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Aatmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan' (Self-Reliant India Campaign) announced in 2020 focused on:
options: Free primary education for all children
Building the country's economic resilience and reducing dependence on imports
questions.correctAnswer: Building the country's economic resilience and reducing dependence on imports
questions.explanation: Aatmanirbhar Bharat (announced May 2020 amid the COVID-19 pandemic) aims to build a self-reliant Indian economy — boosting domestic manufacturing, MSMEs, and reducing import dependence. Free primary education is under RTE Act (2009). Free electricity for farmers is a state-level scheme (varies). A common minimum wage is a separate labour-policy discussion (Code on Wages, 2019).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Consumer Price Index' (CPI) is used to measure:
options: Changes in retail prices of a basket of goods and services
questions.correctAnswer: Changes in retail prices of a basket of goods and services
questions.explanation: CPI measures retail price changes in a fixed basket over time — the RBI now uses CPI as its primary inflation target. WPI (Wholesale Price Index) measures wholesale prices only — a different index. Stock market returns are measured by indices like Sensex/Nifty. Tax collection figures are published by the Ministry of Finance directly.
